name: Greyish hunter green

sections.title: Greyish hunter green is a dark, muted green carried into our library from the Japanese traditional color Chitosemidori, "thousand-year green," a name tied to the pine tree's evergreen symbolism, and it sits 12.4 units from the plain [[hunter-green]].
sections.body:
Our library lists this color under the Japanese name Chitosemidori, written 千歳緑, glossed as "thousand year old green" [1]. *Chitose* (千歳) means a thousand years and *midori* (緑) means green; pine needles, which stay green through winter, carried this association with long life in Japanese design [1]. No book consulted independently confirms the pine link for this specific name, so it is stated here only as the plain meaning of the characters [1].

The swatch measures lightness 27, chroma 12 and hue 133 degrees, in the Greens family, dark and low in saturation, used chiefly in fashion and textile contexts [1]. The nearest named colors on file are [[nickle-green]], [[rifle-green]], [[insect-screen]] and [[vivid-gunmetal]], at 3.8, 3.9, 4.8 and 5 ΔE [1]. A lighter, cooler cousin in the Greens family is [[greenish-sage]] [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: A color within range of this swatch appears in 856 of the 23,781 paintings in our archive, about 3.6 percent, as photographed, most often as a shadow color [2]. The earliest dated match is a 1381 *Virgin and Child* by an unrecorded painter, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2]. Henri Rousseau carries it in 5 of 13 dated paintings, 10.7 times the archive's overall rate [2].

questions.q: True or false: a book consulted for this project confirms a specific link between this name and pine trees.

openers: Greyish hunter green's Japanese name, chitosemidori, literally means "thousand-year green," an association long carried by evergreen pine.

issues: The pine/longevity association is the common gloss for chitose names generally, not confirmed for this swatch specifically by any book consulted; stated plainly as the characters' meaning only.
